methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free AI workshops delivered by a Norfolk native in Hampton Roads represents grassroots, peer-driven capability building outside traditional tech hubs—a concrete signal of distributed, community-led AI literacy development that could spread through non-metro networks.

signals.title: Roanoke College launches WorkAI Lab to prepare leaders for new era of technology - Roanoke College
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke College's WorkAI Lab creates institutional infrastructure for workforce AI training in a non-metro region, suggesting potential for regional depth beyond NoVA if sustained—signals distributed capability building through educational anchors rather than platform-dependent shallow adoption.

signals.title: New Jersey, Virginia Can Lead the Nation By Building ‘AI Resilience Cohorts’ to Develop Early-Career, State Talent Pipelines - Federation of American Scientists
signals.signal_reading: Proposed AI Resilience Cohorts model offers Virginia a mechanism to systematically distribute deep AI talent development across regions through structured early-career pipelines, directly challenging the concentration dynamic if implemented beyond NoVA/Richmond.

signals.title: Left hand, right hand: Virginia cools on data centers even as state policy promotes the AI that requires them - Cardinal News
signals.signal_reading: Virginia's simultaneous promotion of AI policy while local governments resist data center infrastructure reveals a coordination failure that could strand the state between neither achieving distributed capability nor concentrating it effectively—policy incoherence threatens both depth and distribution.

signals.title: In the data center capital of the world, residents ask who the AI boom is helping - NBC News
signals.signal_reading: Residents questioning who benefits from NoVA's data center boom signals that infrastructure concentration is not translating to distributed economic or capability gains—the classic 'infrastructure without inclusion' pattern that reinforces metro-only depth while leaving other regions behind.
